citation: Charbonnier, F.; Morstyn, T.; McCulloch, M. (2023). Home Electricity Data Generator (HEDGE): An open-access tool for the generation of electric vehicle, residential demand, and PV generation profiles. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2310.01661.
description: HEDGE generates synthetic daily profiles of household electricity demand, rooftop photovoltaic output and electric-vehicle consumption and availability. Charbonnier, Morstyn and McCulloch train generative models on UK residential energy and travel data, retaining magnitude and behavioural-cluster consistency across successive days for each home. The Python interface takes a number of homes and returns arrays of energy in kilowatt-hours per interval and binary vehicle availability. Hourly generator inputs are included; other resolutions require a documented preparation stage using the source datasets. Geographic coverage reflects UK training data, not a general global population, and generated days are scenarios, not dated observations. Code is public and free under AGPL 3.0. Preparing travel inputs requires a separate UK Data Service registration, while other source terms remain applicable. No registration was needed to inspect the tool. A limitation is dependence on training-population behaviour and the computational cost of rebuilding the inputs. Simulation uses include residential flexibility, EV charging and control-method benchmarks. It relates to platform-opendss as a potential consumer of generated demand profiles, though conversion and power-flow coupling were not tested.
